title: Periuk Mak Jah
genre: 1950s Malay film-studio orchestral song (P. Ramlee lineage)
mood: sly, comic, polite on top and fed up underneath
subject: a man rehearsing, very politely, how to ask the neighbour to return the rice pot she borrowed three Hari Raya ago
caption: 1950s Malay film-studio orchestral song in the P. Ramlee and Shaw Brothers Jalan Ampas style. A swinging big-band horn section punching short stabs; a muted trumpet answering each vocal line; a violin section playing sweeping runs into the chorus; an upright bass walking; brushed swing drums with a light ride cymbal; a honky-tonk piano comping. Vintage studio sound leaning to mono, slight tape warmth, natural room reverb, bright horns. Male voice, a smooth baritone crooner with theatrical comic timing and short spoken asides. 132 BPM, B-flat major. Sly, comic, polite on top and fed up underneath. No modern drums, no synths, no autotune, no rock guitar, no hip-hop beat.
lyrics:
[Intro - big-band horns and violin run]

[Verse 1]
Selamat petang Mak Jah, cantik bunga kertas
Kucing awak gemuk, rumput pun dah potong
Oh ya, sebelum saya lupa, satu hal kecil
Periuk nasi saya, yang besar warna kelabu

[Pre-Chorus]
Pinjam masa Raya, tiga Raya tak balik-balik

[Chorus]
Periuk Mak Jah, periuk Mak Jah
Dulu periuk saya, sekarang periuk Mak Jah
Tiga kali Raya dah lalu depan pintu
Nasi saya masak dalam kuali, Mak Jah tahu?

[Verse 2]
Saya nampak dari pagar, ada atas dapur
Penuh gulai kawah, wangi sampai ke rumah saya
Mak Jah senyum lebar, hulur semangkuk gulai
Aduh, sedap betul, hilang pula ayat saya

[Pre-Chorus]
Esok saya cuba lagi, hari ini kenyang dulu

[Chorus]
Periuk Mak Jah, periuk Mak Jah
Dulu periuk saya, sekarang periuk Mak Jah
Kalau dia masak gulai sesedap ini
Biarlah periuk tu tinggal, saya datang tiap hari

[Outro - muted trumpet and horn stab]
Mak Jah, esok gulai apa?
